subject: Hosted API: monthly token envelope + burst TPS — post-demo readout
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Grant <elliot@cargomate.ai>, Ruth Park <ruth.park@cargomate.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Demo recap — hosted API fit + traffic shape (follow-up)

Thanks for the time today — great demo, Elliot and Ruth. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

1) What you told us (for accuracy): CargoMate expects to move the summarization + chat routing pipeline to an LLM-backed flow for customer support. Primary targets: reduce handle time for Tier-1 by ~30% and enable extractive summaries for post-call logging.

2) Traffic shape (what we recorded in call):
- Core steady-state: 8–12 TPS (inference requests) during business hours
- Peak windows: two short bursts tied to batch-email sends and midnight ET reruns — observed peak TPS up to ~220 TPS for 3–8 minute windows
- Monthly active token estimate (your current guidance): 12.5M tokens/month (this is the number you mentioned; please confirm)

3) Pricing sensitivity: you called out a budget target in the $30–$40 per 1M-token neighborhood for production (hosted API). You indicated a willingness to consider reserved/dedicated if unit economics improve materially.

4) Proposed next steps:
- Please attach the Q3 forecast (rough daily volumes) so we can model burst/99th TPS and recommend batching/pooling/kv-cache knobs.
- We’ll run a quick unit-econ readout (three scenarios: pay-as-you-go, 6mo commit, 12mo commit) plus an ops playbook for handling the 3–8 minute spikes.
- Karthik, can you own the sample pricing scenarios and a short note on SLA/burst protections?

Attachments: cargo_forecast_Q3_v1.xlsx (please send if you have an updated sheet)

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

From: Elliot Grant <elliot@cargomate.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ruth Park <ruth.park@cargomate.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap — hosted API fit + traffic shape (follow-up)

Thanks Marissa — accurate summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- 12.5M tokens/month is our conservative baseline for July–September if the pilot proves successful; we have upside to ~22M in the event the support AI is rolled out to more product lines.
- The 220 TPS spikes are real and come from two automated jobs we run at 03:00 UTC and again at 15:00 UTC — both are short-lived but hammer the service for ~5 minutes.
- Budget: Ruth and I discussed target $/1M = $35 as a stretch to make the math work internally. We can flex on commit length if the unit price drops.

I’ve attached the Q3 forecast slice (see cargo_forecast_Q3_v1.xlsx) — it’s coarse but shows the daily spikes. Happy to hop on a follow-up if helpful.

Elliot
Head of Platform | CargoMate
elliot@cargomate.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Grant <elliot@cargomate.ai>, Ruth Park <ruth.park@cargomate.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Demo recap — hosted API fit + traffic shape (follow-up)

Appreciate the forecast, Elliot — that helps a lot. Attached is an initial pricing scenarios PDF and a short unit-econ table (redwood_pricing_scenarios.pdf). High-level notes below — I kept the math conservative so it’s aligned with internal procurement expectations.

Scenario A — Pay-as-you-go (no commit):
- Unit price: $58 / 1M tokens
- Monthly cost @12.5M = $725
- No reserved capacity guarantees; autoscaling handles spikes subject to our standard rate-limits and burst queueing (recommend enabling 99th p99 throttling at application layer)

Scenario B — 6-month commit (mid-tier):
- Unit price: $40 / 1M tokens (15% discount applied to list for volume and predictable ramp)
- Monthly cost @12.5M = $500
- We include a 10% reserved burst headroom for 5-minute windows; sustained surplus beyond that can be handled with on-demand scaling (additional charges apply)

Scenario C — 12-month reserved (enterprise commit):
- Unit price: $28 / 1M tokens (lower because of reserved capacity and billing commit)
- Monthly cost @12.5M = $350
- SLA: 99.5% availability for inference endpoints; we provide a predictable burst bucket sized to your 220 TPS 5-minute window when we size dedicated pools to your commit

Quick comments on the math: the price-band you mentioned ($35 target) sits between our 6mo and 12mo offers — we could structure a hybrid (9mo commit at $33 / 1M) to hit your target while giving Redwood some capacity visibility. Karthik, can you confirm whether a 9mo blended commit is operationally feasible?

Operational/engineering notes: 
- For short bursts we recommend: prefix KV caching for repeated context, request batching at the app edge (we can supply middleware examples), and a scheduled jitter on your automated jobs to smooth out simultaneous fan-out.
- If you prefer not to change the job schedule, we’ll size a small reserved burst pool that only becomes active during the 5–8 minute windows and is billed as reserved + small usage surcharge.

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik: pricing confirmation and contract sketch (by Monday).
- Jordan: brief ops note on how we’d throttle and where to set p99 thresholds (I’ll loop him in for a 30m tech readout next week).
- Elliot/Ruth: confirm whether a 9-month blended commit is acceptable, or whether you prefer the 6mo/12mo options.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elliot Grant <elliot@cargomate.ai>, Ruth Park <ruth.park@cargomate.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Demo recap — hosted API fit + traffic shape (follow-up)

Quick operational confirmation from my side:

- 9-month blended commit at $33 / 1M is workable. We’ll size the dedicated reserve pool to cover the 220 TPS 5-minute window assuming 2.5 tokens/tokenization overhead per request (conservative).
- We will include a burst bucket that refills daily for those scheduled jobs; any sustained consumption above the bucket will be billed at the on-demand rate in Scenario A.
- Contract sketch: we’ll propose monthly billing with true-up at 90 days, a 30% ramp protection clause for sudden 3x growth in volume, and an early-exit fee schedule (pro-rated) — draft to follow.

Jordan — can you prepare a 30-minute tech readout template that covers: batch size tuning, KV caching thresholds, and recommended client-side retry/backoff settings so CargoMate can keep p99 latency under 800ms during spikes?

Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
